manifest.json, List of every file in this bundle, what it contains and its SHA-256 checksum. (2 KB)
summary.json, OpenFrame version, Windows version, architecture, distribution channel and database schema versions. (779 bytes)
errors.json, Error codes from recent logs, with how often and when they occurred. (412 bytes)
timings.json, How long slow or failed operations took, by operation name. (119 bytes)
log-tail.txt, The most recent log entries, rebuilt from fixed messages, operation names, error codes and numbers only. (427 bytes)
ai-status.json, Offline AI status: available or not, bundle check, engine state and component versions. No folders or file paths. (1 KB)

Scene 5, INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - STORE ROOM - NIGHT
Scene 6, INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT

Scene 8, EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - CONTINUOUS

Scene 10, EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - DAWN

INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
FADE IN:
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
KIRAN
Did anyone hand in a kite?
DEVI
What kind of kite?
KIRAN
Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
DEVI
No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
He is gone before she can answer.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - PLATFORM 3 - NIGHT
A long platform under yellow lamps. A goods train clanks past without stopping. Kiran sits on a bench with his knees pulled up, watching the sky above the station roof.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The next night. The same knock. Devi does not look up.
DEVI
No kites.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The night after. Devi already has her finger on the register when the knock comes.
DEVI
(before he speaks)
Still no kites.
KIRAN
How do you know I came for the kite?
DEVI
Nobody comes three nights in a row for a shoe.
He almost smiles. Then he goes.
Devi watches the empty window. She closes the register.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - STORE ROOM - NIGHT
A long, low room under the platforms. Cages of sacks and crates. A single TUBE LIGHT that buzzes and flickers.
Devi walks along the shelves with a TORCH. She lifts tarpaulins, opens crates, moves a broken harmonium.
Behind a stack of suitcases, something red. She pulls it free.
A KITE, its frame snapped in two places, the paper torn. The newspaper tail is tangled around a suitcase handle. On the back, in marker: KIRAN.
DEVI
(to herself)
You were hiding.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The kite lies on the counter. Devi sits with a pot of GLUE, a roll of TAPE and two thin BAMBOO STICKS cut from a broom.
She splints the frame. She patches the tear with a page from the register, the blank side out. Her hands know the work.
The knock. Kiran sees the kite. He grips the bars.
KIRAN
That is mine.
DEVI
I know. Your name is on it.
KIRAN
It is broken.
DEVI
It was broken. Now it is mended. Those are different.
She slides it under the bars. He holds it as if it might break again.
KIRAN
My father made it. Before he went to work in the city.
DEVI
Then he will want to know it still flies.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - NIGHT
The footbridge over the tracks. Wind rattles the iron railings. Kiran and Devi climb the steps, Devi slower, one hand on the rail.
DEVI
I am not running. Do not ask me to run.
KIRAN
You do not have to run. You only have to hold it up.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - CONTINUOUS
Devi holds the kite high over her head. Kiran walks backwards, paying out the string from a SPOOL.
KIRAN
Let go!
She lets go. The kite dips toward the tracks, then catches the wind and climbs.
It rises over the station roof, the newspaper tail snapping behind it. Kiran laughs out loud.
A night train slides beneath them, every window lit. Passengers look up.
INT. NIGHT TRAIN - SECOND CLASS COMPARTMENT - CONTINUOUS
A tired MAN (30s, work clothes, lunch tin on his lap) looks out of the window. He sees a red kite above the station. He sits up.
He presses his hand flat against the glass.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - DAWN
Grey light. The kite still flies. Kiran sits on the bridge floor with the string tied around his wrist, asleep against the railing.
Devi sits beside him, peanuts in her lap. She takes out the REGISTER and writes in her slow, neat capitals:
INSERT - THE REGISTER
"ONE KITE. RED. RETURNED TO OWNER."
BACK TO SCENE
She closes the book and looks up at the kite.
FADE

INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
FADE IN:
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
KIRAN
Did anyone hand in a kite?
DEVI
What kind of kite?
KIRAN
Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
DEVI
No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
He is gone before she can answer.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - PLATFORM 3 - NIGHT
A long platform under yellow lamps. A goods train clanks past without stopping. Kiran sits on a bench with his knees pulled up, watching the sky above the station roof.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The next night. The same knock. Devi does not look up.
DEVI
No kites.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The night after. Devi already has her finger on the register when the knock comes.
DEVI
(before he speaks)
Still no kites.
KIRAN
How do you know I came for the kite?
DEVI
Nobody comes three nights in a row for a shoe.
He almost smiles. Then he goes.
Devi watches the empty window. She closes the register.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - STORE ROOM - NIGHT
A long, low room under the platforms. Cages of sacks and crates. A single TUBE LIGHT that buzzes and flickers.
Devi walks along the shelves with a TORCH. She lifts tarpaulins, opens crates, moves a broken harmonium.
Behind a stack of suitcases, something red. She pulls it free.
A KITE, its frame snapped in two places, the paper torn. The newspaper tail is tangled around a suitcase handle. On the back, in marker: KIRAN.
DEVI
(to herself)
You were hiding.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The kite lies on the counter. Devi sits with a pot of GLUE, a roll of TAPE and two thin BAMBOO STICKS cut from a broom.
She splints the frame. She patches the tear with a page from the register, the blank side out. Her hands know the work.
The knock. Kiran sees the kite. He grips the bars.
KIRAN
That is mine.
DEVI
I know. Your name is on it.
KIRAN
It is broken.
DEVI
It was broken. Now it is mended. Those are different.
She slides it under the bars. He holds it as if it might break again.
KIRAN
My father made it. Before he went to work in the city.
DEVI
Then he will want to know it still flies.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - NIGHT
The footbridge over the tracks. Wind rattles the iron railings. Kiran and Devi climb the steps, Devi slower, one hand on the rail.
DEVI
I am not running. Do not ask me to run.
KIRAN
You do not have to run. You only have to hold it up.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - CONTINUOUS
Devi holds the kite high over her head. Kiran walks backwards, paying out the string from a SPOOL.
KIRAN
Let go!
She lets go. The kite dips toward the tracks, then catches the wind and climbs.
It rises over the station roof, the newspaper tail snapping behind it. Kiran laughs out loud.
A night train slides beneath them, every window lit. Passengers look up.
INT. NIGHT TRAIN - SECOND CLASS COMPARTMENT - CONTINUOUS
A tired MAN (30s, work clothes, lunch tin on his lap) looks out of the window. He sees a red kite above the station. He sits up.
He presses his hand flat against the glass.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - DAWN
Grey light. The kite still flies. Kiran sits on the bridge floor with the string tied around his wrist, asleep against the railing.
Devi sits beside him, peanuts in her lap. She takes out the REGISTER and writes in her slow, neat capitals:
INSERT - THE REGISTER
"ONE KITE. RED. RETURNED TO OWNER."
BACK TO SCENE
She closes the book and looks up at the kite.
FADE

INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
FADE IN:
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
KIRAN
Did anyone hand in a kite?
DEVI
What kind of kite?
KIRAN
Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
DEVI
No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
He is gone before she can answer.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - PLATFORM 3 - NIGHT
A long platform under yellow lamps. A goods train clanks past without stopping. Kiran sits on a bench with his knees pulled up, watching the sky above the station roof.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The next night. The same knock. Devi does not look up.
DEVI
No kites.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The night after. Devi already has her finger on the register when the knock comes.
DEVI
(before he speaks)
Still no kites.
KIRAN
How do you know I came for the kite?
DEVI
Nobody comes three nights in a row for a shoe.
He almost smiles. Then he goes.
Devi watches the empty window. She closes the register.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - STORE ROOM - NIGHT
A long, low room under the platforms. Cages of sacks and crates. A single TUBE LIGHT that buzzes and flickers.
Devi walks along the shelves with a TORCH. She lifts tarpaulins, opens crates, moves a broken harmonium.
Behind a stack of suitcases, something red. She pulls it free.
A KITE, its frame snapped in two places, the paper torn. The newspaper tail is tangled around a suitcase handle. On the back, in marker: KIRAN.
DEVI
(to herself)
You were hiding.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The kite lies on the counter. Devi sits with a pot of GLUE, a roll of TAPE and two thin BAMBOO STICKS cut from a broom.
She splints the frame. She patches the tear with a page from the register, the blank side out. Her hands know the work.
The knock. Kiran sees the kite. He grips the bars.
KIRAN
That is mine.
DEVI
I know. Your name is on it.
KIRAN
It is broken.
DEVI
It was broken. Now it is mended. Those are different.
She slides it under the bars. He holds it as if it might break again.
KIRAN
My father made it. Before he went to work in the city.
DEVI
Then he will want to know it still flies.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - NIGHT
The footbridge over the tracks. Wind rattles the iron railings. Kiran and Devi climb the steps, Devi slower, one hand on the rail.
DEVI
I am not running. Do not ask me to run.
KIRAN
You do not have to run. You only have to hold it up.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - CONTINUOUS
Devi holds the kite high over her head. Kiran walks backwards, paying out the string from a SPOOL.
KIRAN
Let go!
She lets go. The kite dips toward the tracks, then catches the wind and climbs.
It rises over the station roof, the newspaper tail snapping behind it. Kiran laughs out loud.
A night train slides beneath them, every window lit. Passengers look up.
INT. NIGHT TRAIN - SECOND CLASS COMPARTMENT - CONTINUOUS
A tired MAN (30s, work clothes, lunch tin on his lap) looks out of the window. He sees a red kite above the station. He sits up.
He presses his hand flat against the glass.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - DAWN
Grey light. The kite still flies. Kiran sits on the bridge floor with the string tied around his wrist, asleep against the railing.
Devi sits beside him, peanuts in her lap. She takes out the REGISTER and writes in her slow, neat capitals:
INSERT - THE REGISTER
"ONE KITE. RED. RETURNED TO OWNER."
BACK TO SCENE
She closes the book and looks up at the kite.
FADE

1  INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
FADE IN:
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
KIRAN
Did anyone hand in a kite?
DEVI
What kind of kite?
KIRAN
Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
DEVI
No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
He is gone before she can answer.

1  INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
FADE IN:
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
KIRAN
Did anyone hand in a kite?
DEVI
What kind of kite?
KIRAN
Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
DEVI
No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
He is gone before she can answer.
Wears the school bag in every scene

Scene 2, EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - PLATFORM 3 - NIGHT
Scene 3, INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
Scene 4, INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
Scene 5, INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - STORE ROOM - NIGHT
Scene 6, INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
Scene 7, EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - NIGHT
Scene 8, EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - CONTINUOUS
Scene 9, INT. NIGHT TRAIN - SECOND CLASS COMPARTMENT - CONTINUOUS
Scene 10, EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - DAWN

INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
FADE IN:
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
KIRAN
Did anyone hand in a kite?
DEVI
What kind of kite?
KIRAN
Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
DEVI
No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
He is gone before she can answer.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - PLATFORM 3 - NIGHT
A long platform under yellow lamps. A goods train clanks past without stopping. Kiran sits on a bench with his knees pulled up, watching the sky above the station roof.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The next night. The same knock. Devi does not look up.
DEVI
No kites.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The night after. Devi already has her finger on the register when the knock comes.
DEVI
(before he speaks)
Still no kites.
KIRAN
How do you know I came for the kite?
DEVI
Nobody comes three nights in a row for a shoe.
He almost smiles. Then he goes.
Devi watches the empty window. She closes the register.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - STORE ROOM - NIGHT
A long, low room under the platforms. Cages of sacks and crates. A single TUBE LIGHT that buzzes and flickers.
Devi walks along the shelves with a TORCH. She lifts tarpaulins, opens crates, moves a broken harmonium.
Behind a stack of suitcases, something red. She pulls it free.
A KITE, its frame snapped in two places, the paper torn. The newspaper tail is tangled around a suitcase handle. On the back, in marker: KIRAN.
DEVI
(to herself)
You were hiding.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The kite lies on the counter. Devi sits with a pot of GLUE, a roll of TAPE and two thin BAMBOO STICKS cut from a broom.
She splints the frame. She patches the tear with a page from the register, the blank side out. Her hands know the work.
The knock. Kiran sees the kite. He grips the bars.
KIRAN
That is mine.
DEVI
I know. Your name is on it.
KIRAN
It is broken.
DEVI
It was broken. Now it is mended. Those are different.
She slides it under the bars. He holds it as if it might break again.
KIRAN
My father made it. Before he went to work in the city.
DEVI
Then he will want to know it still flies.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - NIGHT
The footbridge over the tracks. Wind rattles the iron railings. Kiran and Devi climb the steps, Devi slower, one hand on the rail.
DEVI
I am not running. Do not ask me to run.
KIRAN
You do not have to run. You only have to hold it up.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - CONTINUOUS
Devi holds the kite high over her head. Kiran walks backwards, paying out the string from a SPOOL.
KIRAN
Let go!
She lets go. The kite dips toward the tracks, then catches the wind and climbs.
It rises over the station roof, the newspaper tail snapping behind it. Kiran laughs out loud.
A night train slides beneath them, every window lit. Passengers look up.
INT. NIGHT TRAIN - SECOND CLASS COMPARTMENT - CONTINUOUS
A tired MAN (30s, work clothes, lunch tin on his lap) looks out of the window. He sees a red kite above the station. He sits up.
He presses his hand flat against the glass.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - DAWN
Grey light. The kite still flies. Kiran sits on the bridge floor with the string tied around his wrist, asleep against the railing.
Devi sits beside him, peanuts in her lap. She takes out the REGISTER and writes in her slow, neat capitals:
INSERT - THE REGISTER
"ONE KITE. RED. RETURNED TO OWNER."
BACK TO SCENE
She closes the book and looks up at the kite.
FADE

(to herself)

INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
FADE IN:
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
KIRAN
Did anyone hand in a kite?
DEVI
What kind of kite?
KIRAN
Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
DEVI
No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
He is gone before she can answer.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - PLATFORM 3 - NIGHT
A long platform under yellow lamps. A goods train clanks past without stopping. Kiran sits on a bench with his knees pulled up, watching the sky above the station roof.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The next night. The same knock. Devi does not look up.
DEVI
No kites.
KIRAN
I will come tomorrow.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The night after. Devi already has her finger on the register when the knock comes.
DEVI
(before he speaks)
Still no kites.
KIRAN
How do you know I came for the kite?
DEVI
Nobody comes three nights in a row for a shoe.
He almost smiles. Then he goes.
Devi watches the empty window. She closes the register.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - STORE ROOM - NIGHT
A long, low room under the platforms. Cages of sacks and crates. A single TUBE LIGHT that buzzes and flickers.
Devi walks along the shelves with a TORCH. She lifts tarpaulins, opens crates, moves a broken harmonium.
Behind a stack of suitcases, something red. She pulls it free.
A KITE, its frame snapped in two places, the paper torn. The newspaper tail is tangled around a suitcase handle. On the back, in marker: KIRAN.
DEVI
(to herself)
You were hiding.
INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
The kite lies on the counter. Devi sits with a pot of GLUE, a roll of TAPE and two thin BAMBOO STICKS cut from a broom.
She splints the frame. She patches the tear with a page from the register, the blank side out. Her hands know the work.
The knock. Kiran sees the kite. He grips the bars.
KIRAN
That is mine.
DEVI
I know. Your name is on it.
KIRAN
It is broken.
DEVI
It was broken. Now it is mended. Those are different.
She slides it under the bars. He holds it as if it might break again.
KIRAN
My father made it. Before he went to work in the city.
DEVI
Then he will want to know it still flies.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - NIGHT
The footbridge over the tracks. Wind rattles the iron railings. Kiran and Devi climb the steps, Devi slower, one hand on the rail.
DEVI
I am not running. Do not ask me to run.
KIRAN
You do not have to run. You only have to hold it up.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - CONTINUOUS
Devi holds the kite high over her head. Kiran walks backwards, paying out the string from a SPOOL.
KIRAN
Let go!
She lets go. The kite dips toward the tracks, then catches the wind and climbs.
It rises over the station roof, the newspaper tail snapping behind it. Kiran laughs out loud.
A night train slides beneath them, every window lit. Passengers look up.
INT. NIGHT TRAIN - SECOND CLASS COMPARTMENT - CONTINUOUS
A tired MAN (30s, work clothes, lunch tin on his lap) looks out of the window. He sees a red kite above the station. He sits up.
He presses his hand flat against the glass.
EXT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - FOOTBRIDGE - DAWN
Grey light. The kite still flies. Kiran sits on the bridge floor with the string tied around his wrist, asleep against the railing.
Devi sits beside him, peanuts in her lap. She takes out the REGISTER and writes in her slow, neat capitals:
INSERT - THE REGISTER
"ONE KITE. RED. RETURNED TO OWNER."
BACK TO SCENE
She closes the book and looks up at the kite.
FADE
